analysis:
Docs-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. I examined both head_text units (lines 1-415 and 416-798). Neither contains the hunk at head lines 1050-1070, so the paged-KV segment parking paragraph is only visible as a truncated patch excerpt; its source citations are cut off mid-path.

The visible change is the added eviction text (head ~404-410): the Nemotron Super load gate now first releases retained free KV segments and drops MLX's buffer cache once via `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad`, and pre-accept counts retained segments as reachable. This describes memory-reclaim behavior and does not touch the coordinator/provider WebSocket, attestation, key handling or E2E encryption.

The truncated paragraph describes parking released free 64 MiB KV segments per pool, up to min(2 GiB, grant/8), outside the grant and ledger charge, and reinstalling them for the next same-size admission. It also describes zero-fill-on-demand host pages for new segments. The prose does not say whether parked segments are zeroed or scoped between requests/tenants. This touches T-028 (residual GPU/KV data) and T-041 (cross-tenant cache). Segments are reused without scrubbing across requests, but that is a code-level question, and no code is supplied in this batch. The existing T-028 already accepts residual KV data until overwritten, so I report no finding.

Open integration question: if the corresponding Swift code is in another batch, check that parked segments cannot leak stale KV contents across cache scopes. Check that the parked memory is accounted for under the memory-pressure and DoS posture (T-016/T-029 style). Also check that the doc claim of outside-ledger memory matches the implementation. No security regression is evidenced by the doc text alone.
